stem: An investor buys a stock at USD 50 using 40% initial margin. The maintenance margin is 30%. The price below which the investor receives a margin call is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. This is 50 × (1 − 0.30), which applies the maintenance margin to the purchase price instead of solving the equity condition.
rationale.B: Correct. The loan per share is 30; equity equals 30% of value when P − 30 = 0.30P, giving P = 42.86.
rationale.C: Incorrect. This is 50 × 0.40/0.70, which uses the initial margin instead of (1 − initial margin) in the numerator.

stem: An investor buys one share at USD 25 with 40% initial margin and borrows the rest at 6% a year. The stock pays no dividend and there are no commissions. One year later the share is sold for USD 27.50. The return on the investor's equity is closest to:
explanation: Equity = 10, loan = 15, interest = 0.90. Ending equity = 27.50 − 15 − 0.90 = 11.60. Return = 11.60/10 − 1 = 16.00%.

rationale.A: Incorrect. This is the 10% price change times the 2.5 leverage ratio, ignoring the 0.90 of interest on the margin loan.
rationale.B: Incorrect. This is the unleveraged price return of the stock.
rationale.C: Correct. After repaying the 15 loan and 0.90 interest, equity grows from 10 to 11.60, a 16.00% return.

stem: A trader holds a stock trading at USD 80 and wants to limit losses if the price falls sharply, while staying invested if the price rises. Which order best meets this goal?
options: A limit sell order at USD 85
A stop-loss sell order at USD 72
explanation: A stop-loss sell order becomes active only if the price trades down to the stop level, so the position is kept on the upside and exited on a fall.

rationale.A: Incorrect. A limit sell at 85 exits the position on a rise, which locks in gains but does nothing to protect against a fall.
rationale.B: Correct. The stop order sits below the market and triggers a sale only if the price falls to 72, capping the loss (though the fill may be below 72).
rationale.C: Incorrect. A market sell exits immediately, so the trader gives up any upside.

stem: In a market where all participants submit orders to a central book that matches buyers and sellers by price priority and then time priority, the market is best described as:
explanation: Order-driven markets match public orders using rules such as price and time priority; no dealer has to stand on the other side.

rationale.A: Correct. A central limit order book with matching rules is the defining feature of an order-driven market.
rationale.B: Incorrect. In a quote-driven market investors trade against dealers' posted bid and ask prices.
rationale.C: Incorrect. Brokered markets rely on brokers searching for counterparties, typically for unique or illiquid assets.
